deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.1, 23.12.83). Σ is a nontrivial system of pseudolines in the projective plane X, with vertex set S. P = PR(Σ) is the set of relative positions (isotopy classes) of one additional pseudoline D, that is, the one-element extensions Σ' = Σ ∪ {D}.

The structure from p.1:
- An immediate specialization D → D' is given by a 'specialization triangle' T. Its apex is a vertex s of Σ of order ν. Its base is an arc of D̃, where D̃ is the circle of 'rives' (banks) of D: the boundary of a Möbius-band neighbourhood of D, a double cover of D with a polygonal structure. The triangle contains no other vertex of Σ.
- D' is obtained by pushing D across s.
- These arrows form a strict oriented graph Γ(Σ) with vertex set P (the injectivity of P̃ → P×P is proved on p.1).
- Gn_0(D) is the set of immediate generizations: pairs (s, s̃) with s ∈ S∩D and s̃ one of the two points of D̃ over s.

This page:
(1) Each element of Sp_0(D) determines an open arc of D̃, and these arcs are pairwise disjoint. Each element of Gn_0(D) determines a point of D̃; these points are distinct and lie outside the arcs. Hence the set Sp_0(D) ⊔ Gn_0(D) of all edges of Γ at the vertex D inherits a cyclic ('polygonal') order. In modern terms, Γ(Σ) becomes a ribbon graph (a map, i.e. a graph with rotation system), the natural first step toward showing that P is the vertex set of a 2-dimensional cell structure on a surface.
(2) Conjecture: every vertex has degree at least 3, so that the local polygons are non-degenerate.
- If |S∩D| ≥ 2 there are already at least 4 generizations, two points of D̃ over each vertex.
- Stable case (|S∩D| = 0): one needs 3 distinct specialization triangles.
- Semi-stable case (|S∩D| = 1): there are 2 generizations, so one needs 1 specialization.
(3a) Stable case proof.
- By Levi's theorem, D is adjacent to at least 3 triangles of Σ'.
- Pick one; it lies in a unique specialization triangle T (apex s, base t–v on D).
- T determines two 'big triangles' A and B (see the figure) on either side.
- In each of them there is at least one triangle of Σ' adjacent to D, lying in a unique specialization triangle T', resp. T''.
- This yields T, T', T''.
(3b) Semi-stable case begun: a is the unique vertex on D; consider a specialization D' in which a 'slides' along an edge bc. The argument breaks off.

On p.3 Grothendieck finds a counterexample (Σ = St_{4,3}?) and realizes that the positions D = Δ ∈ Σ themselves ('surconstrictive' positions) were omitted. Specializations into them happen through 'cuvettes', which count as specialization triangles.

The programme: describe the space of one-element extensions of a pseudoline arrangement as a cell complex with explicit local structure. In the realizable case this is the cell decomposition of the dual plane X* by the lines dual to the vertices of Σ, plus the points dual to the lines of Σ. Γ records specialization (face-type) incidences, and the cyclic orders are the local surface structure.
errors: The degree ≥3 claim, as formulated with P consisting only of positions distinct from the lines of Σ, is false in the semi-stable case. Grothendieck himself finds a counterexample on the next page and repairs it by adding the positions D = Δ ∈ Σ and 'cuvettes of specialization'.

Stable case: distinctness of T, T', T'' is asserted via the figure (big triangles A and B) but not fully argued. One must check that the triangles of Σ' adjacent to D found in A and in B cannot lie in T or in a common specialization triangle. Plausible, but a gap as written.
Use of Levi's 3-triangle theorem requires Σ' nontrivial (not a pencil); this is covered by the exclusion of trivial Σ on p.1.
Semi-stable case is left unfinished on this page.

ideas.what: Cyclic (polygonal) order on the set of edges of the specialization graph Γ(Σ) at each position D, obtained from disjoint arcs and points on the double-cover circle D̃
ideas.modern_name: Rotation system / ribbon-graph structure on the Hasse-type diagram of the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Extension spaces: Las Vergnas (single-element extensions, 1978), Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993, rank 3 extension space ≃ S^2)

ideas.what: Positions of an added pseudoline classified by |S∩D| (stable = 0, semi-stable = 1, ≥2), with specialization = passing through a vertex
ideas.modern_name: Cells of the extension space / dual arrangement (topes, edges, vertices of the dual cell complex)

ideas.what: Every pseudoline of a nontrivial arrangement is adjacent to at least 3 triangles
Lower bound ≥3 on the degree of each vertex of Γ(Σ) (local non-degeneracy of the polygonal structure)
ideas.modern_name: Local manifold / regular-cell condition for the extension space

missed.claim: Grothendieck equips the graph of one-element extensions of a pseudoline arrangement with a cyclic order at each vertex, aiming at a surface (cellular) structure on the extension space. This anticipates the rank-3 extension space theorem of Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993, homotopy type S^2), and suggests a more combinatorial, map-theoretic (dessin/carte-style) route to an actual surface structure (RP^2 in the unoriented setting).
missed.quote: Il en résulte une structure polygonale sur l'ens. Sp_0(D) ⨿ Gn_0(D), qui s'identifie aussi à l'ens. des arcs issus du sommet D du graphe Γ(Σ).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A ribbon-graph description of the rank-3 extension space, with explicit local polygons, would give a direct proof that it is a closed surface rather than just homotopy-equivalent to a sphere. It could also link pseudoline combinatorics to Grothendieck's theory of maps.

missed.claim: Degree ≥3 for every vertex of Γ(Σ) is proved for stable positions only. The semi-stable case is abandoned and corrected on p.3 by enlarging P with the lines of Σ ('cuvettes').
missed.quote: Cet ens. a au moins trois éléments je crois.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Pins down which degenerate (non-simple, parallel-element) extensions must be included for the extension space to be a regular cell complex. This is a subtle point in extension-space theory.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, independent and early (1983) combinatorial study of the space of single-pseudoline extensions with a local cyclic-order structure, anticipating rank-3 extension-space results. Nothing here is beyond what Sturmfels–Ziegler and others later did, and the page is partly erroneous and unfinished.
transcription_corrections: 'Cerc_0(D)' should read 'Gn_0(D)' (immediate generizations), consistent with the previous page.
Figure labels in the upper right: big triangles labelled A and B, apex s, base points t and v on the green line D.
'adjacents le long de l'arc extérieur (t, v) au (s, v) et à (s, t)' is likely 'adjacents à T le long de l'arête (s,v) et (s,t)' (the big triangles A and B adjoin T along its two sides); uncertain.
Margin addition in (a), 'immédiats voisins[?]', is uncertain; the sense is that in each of A and B there is a triangle of Σ' adjacent to D.
